page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor offering 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores via multithreading. Compute resources are coupled with 32 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Local storage is directly integrated into the instance, featuring a 322 GB local solid-state drive alongside support for remote Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance firmly in the mid-range across standard general-purpose metrics. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1196.0 and a multi-core score of 4470.0, paired with an overall PassMark CPU score of 8550.46. Memory throughput is solid, recording 50.58 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 36.95 GB/sec in writes. Synthetic tests reveal performance tradeoffs: while multi-core stress testing and Clang compilation test results sit in the middle tier, single-core stress-ng tests and multithreaded bzip3 decompression place in the lower quartile.

With balanced CPU-to-memory density and integrated local SSD capacity, the D8ds_v4 delivers balanced resource allocation without requiring dedicated GPU acceleration. This profile makes it functionally efficient for middle-tier enterprise applications, static web serving, Redis caching, microservices architectures, and relational database servers that benefit from high-speed temporary scratch disk space.
description: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32 GB of RAM, and a bundled 322 GB local SSD. Its hardware architecture includes vector instruction support via AVX-512 alongside standard AES encryption acceleration. In synthetic benchmarks, the D8ds_v4 displays consistent middle-tier performance, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 4470.0, PassMark CPU score of 8550.46, and Redis throughput of 7.33 million operations per second. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 50.58 GB/sec, while web serving delivers 7.25 GB/sec. The instance delivers a balanced resource distribution suited for containerized workloads, web servers, backend application hosting, and database engines requiring fast local temporary storage.
